text:
Brett Howden is playing a bigger role than his reputation suggests. He has 7 goals in 24 games for Vegas, already more than half of last season's 12, and he has done it largely as a finisher: Jesse Granger of The Athletic described Jack Eichel setting him up on Nov. 18 with a no-look backhand from behind the net, and two nights later Jake Oettinger had to rob him on a two-on-one with Eichel.

The goals are real. His 6.7 expected goals on his own shots, the quality-of-chance measure, nearly match his 7 goals, and his chance rate of 1.1 per 60 is almost double last season's. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of the best passes last season (1.6 shots per 60 off cross-slot or behind-the-net passes).

Where he has been unlucky is everything around the goals. Vegas has scored 8.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and he has just 3 assists. We flag him as due for that to swing back. He has 2 goals and no assists over his last ten games, below the 4.2 points we'd expect.
headline: Finishing what Eichel starts
